subject: FinPay: Hosted vs Dedicated decision — latency & throughput follow-up
messages:
From: Sarah Johnson <sarah.johnson@finpay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Lee <tom.lee@finpay.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Intro + latency/throughput needs

Thanks Marissa — good call today. Quick recap from our side:

- Use case: real-time fraud insights in checkout flow (single-turn prompts, low token counts ~60-128 tokens)
- Peak traffic: ~350-400 QPS globally (US primary)
- Latency SLO: p95 under 300ms end-to-end ideally, median ~100-150ms
- Data sensitivity: PII in the payload but no long-term storage; must meet standard SOC2 controls; may need VPC if required by procurement

We heard that Redwood has Hosted API and Dedicated options. Given our p95 requirement at 400 QPS, we're worried about variability on shared hosted infrastructure. Can you confirm whether Hosted would meet our p95 and what the Dedicated sizing looks like? Also please share a quick procurement checklist for Dedicated.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Johnson
Head of Product, FinPay
sarah.johnson@finpay.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Johnson <sarah.johnson@finpay.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-02T09:28:00-08:00
Subject: FinPay: Hosted vs Dedicated — initial sizing & next steps

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear recap and for joining the call.

Short answers up front:
- Hosted API: great for fast time-to-value and lower cost. For sustained 400 QPS with p95 <300ms we generally recommend Dedicated — Hosted can handle bursty traffic but p95 can vary depending on load and tenant co-location.
- Dedicated: gives predictable throughput, reserved GPU pools, and SLA support. We'll size nodes based on model and avg token length; initial estimate below.

Initial sizing (ballpark):
- Model assumption: a 13B parameter model quantized (common for NLU prompts at 60-128 tokens)
- Throughput: ~150-200 QPS per A100-80GB-equivalent node at p95 ~120-250ms depending on batching and token count
- For 400 QPS peak: recommend 3 nodes (reserve 1 for failover/burst). That maps to a Dedicated pool of 3x80GB GPUs (~SLA-backed)

Next steps I propose:
1) Dev-led throughput test: you send a 10-minute traffic sample (we can replay) — Dev will run against a Hosted test endpoint and a Dedicated test pool to show p95/median.
2) PoC: 2-week Dedicated trial with instrumentation and dashboards (cost estimate attached).
3) Procurement checklist & contract redlines (I'll loop legal/finance after we confirm PoC).

I've attached a sample throughput CSV you can send us, plus a sizing estimate and PoC test plan. Dev — can you confirm the test configuration and available windows?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachments: FinPay_throughput_sample_20261201.csv; Redwood_Dedicated_Sizing_Estimate_20261202.pdf; PoC_Test_Plan_20261203.docx

Subject: Re: FinPay: Hosted vs Dedicated — test config

Hi Sarah — thanks for the data in advance. Quick technical notes:

Planned test config:
- Replay your 10-minute sample at scaled rates to recreate peak and 1.5x burst scenarios.
- Test both Hosted test endpoint (shared pool) and a Dedicated 3-node pool.
- Measure p50/p95/p99 latency, token throughput, request error rates, and CPU/GPU utilization.
- We'll run with batching disabled first to measure cold single-request latency, then enable adaptive batching to simulate production.

Expected outcomes:
- Hosted: should show median ~80-160ms for 60-128 tokens but p95 may exceed 300ms under sustained 400 QPS depending on co-tenancy.
- Dedicated (3x80GB equiv): expect p95 in the 150-280ms range for your token profile; with tuning (KV caching/prefix batching) we can push p95 lower.

Schedule:
- When can you provide the sample? We can run tests starting Tuesday 2026-12-08 and share results same day.

I'll also attach the PoC test plan and a preliminary cost estimate for a 2-week Dedicated trial.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
